title: Quarterly Services Report (Third Quarter 2026) — the full QSS release that seasonally adjusts the subsector detail the 11-19 advance publishes raw, 10:00 a.m. ET
source: CENSUS: two independent census.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research, both naming the date. (1) services/release_schedule.html, the QSS program's OWN schedule table headed "2025/2026 Release Schedule for the Advance Quarterly Services Report and the Quarterly Services Report — All releases occur at 10 am", whose "2026 Quarter 3" row reads "Thursday, December 10, 2026" in the Quarterly Services Report column (the same row's advance column reads "Thursday, November 19, 2026"; the "2025 Quarter 3" row reads "Suspended | Thursday, December 11, 2025"). (2) economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes, 179 rows parsed), row "Quarterly Services Survey | December 10, 2026 | 10:00 AM | Third Quarter 2026", release code A202612101000, reference A202603. Promoted estimate -> confirmed and EST: -> CENSUS: on the two-primary precedent this calendar already carries for advance-services-q3-2026-11-19, housing-starts-2026-12-17, m3-full-report-2026-12-03 and durable-goods-2026-11-25. Confirmed is a claim about the SCHEDULED DATE: this half of the series has never been suspended in 28 scheduled rows 2020-2026 (the advance half has, once), and 2026-12-10 falls one day INSIDE the funded window that cr-expiry-2026-12-11 closes. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-06) after reading its one proposal, `from-advance-services-q3-2026-11-19`, which is now shadowed. The proposal's frame — this release is the scoring date for the advance's own number — is SUPPORTED but its stated bound is wrong, and three findings of this session correct or sharpen it. (1) THE ADVANCE->FULL BOUND IS 0.20pp, NOT 0.10pp, AND THE BREACH IS THE MOST RECENT PAIR. The Q1 2026 full report (2026-06-11, fetched from a Wayback capture of services/qss/qss-current.pdf) states verbatim: "The fourth quarter of 2025 to first quarter of 2026 percentage change was revised from the advance estimate of 0.9 percent (+/-0.4 percent)" against its own headline of +1.1 percent — a 0.20pp revision, double the maximum in the 12-pair sample the proposal and the sibling ledger both cite, and the newest completed pair on record. (2) WHAT THE FULL REPORT ACTUALLY ADDS is seasonal adjustment of the SUBSECTORS, not a second look at the headline. Verified word-for-word across two advance captures and three full captures: an advance prints "Advance U.S. utilities total revenue ... NOT adjusted for seasonal variation or price changes", the full report prints "U.S. utilities revenue ... ADJUSTED for seasonal variation but not for price changes". Only the Selected Services Total is seasonally adjusted in an advance. That is why 12-10 matters after the 11-19 AIES benchmark: it is the first release to apply Census's new seasonal factors to the subsector detail. (3) THE CORRIDOR IS THE WHOLE STORY. 2026-12-10 is CPI day (cpi-2026-12-10, high, confirmed, 08:30 ET — 90 minutes before this 10:00 print), the day after fomc-2026-12-09 (high, confirmed), and the day before cr-expiry-2026-12-11. That is not a coincidence of one quarter: across 26 realized full-report dates 2020-2026 the QSS full report shares its session with CPI or PPI 15 times, against 1 of 26 for the advance. Impact LOW and symbols empty on measured grounds: 0 of 1,871 GDPNow vintages 2014-05-01 -> 2026-07-28 name this survey, the Atlanta Fed posts no vintage on 2026-12-10, and a re-grep of trade-playbooks.md + multi-symbol-sweep.md returns 0 macro- or services-keyed hits. Date confirmed; nothing here licenses an entry.
